key_insight: Metal Sandbox combines isolated file access with native macOS command execution to support concurrent AI agents writing Apple Metal GPU kernels. Its scheduling approach targets GPU time left idle while agents wait for model responses or run development commands.
problem_solved: GPU coding agents alternate between model requests, development tasks, and GPU execution, leaving accelerators underused. Running multiple agents concurrently also requires separating their files while preserving access to native Apple Silicon tools.
method: Restrict file access per instance to isolate concurrent agent sessions.
Execute development commands natively on macOS for Apple Metal kernel workflows.
Introduce command-level scheduling; the supplied abstract ends before describing its mechanism or evaluation.
impact: This infrastructure could make training and evaluating Metal kernel–generating agents more efficient on Apple Silicon. The supplied abstract does not report measured utilization gains or performance results.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing isolated agent workspaces connected to native macOS tools and a shared Apple Silicon GPU.
Agent timeline separating model requests, development commands, and GPU execution, with idle gaps highlighted.
Conceptual scheduling diagram showing GPU tasks from multiple agents interleaved on one accelerator.
Shield, terminal, and GPU icons representing isolation, native execution, and accelerator access.
paper_title: Metal Sandbox: Isolated Execution and Command Scheduling for GPU Coding Agents on Apple Silicon
paper_authors: Haozhe Wang, Lina Chen, Fanqi Wan, Qi Han, Yinmin Zhang
